title: B1 · L18 — Past obligation & absence
topic: Past obligation: had to, didn't have to, shouldn't have
description: Cómo expresar obligación, ausencia de obligación y arrepentimiento en el pasado: had to, didn't have to, should/shouldn't have.

questions.prompt: Recuerdas las normas estrictas de tu infancia en casa.
questions.question: Complete: 'When I was a child, I ___ eat all my vegetables.'
questions.explanation: 'Had to' → forma pasada de 'must' y 'have to' para obligación. 'Must' NO tiene forma pasada propia. Error típico del hispanohablante: 'musted' (no existe) o 'had must' (imposible). Regla clave: para hablar de obligaciones pasadas, siempre 'had to'.
examples: I had to work late yesterday — nightmare deadline. → obligación pasada
We had to walk home because there were no buses. → necesidad pasada

questions.prompt: Cuentas cómo tu jefe pagó la comida de un cliente.
questions.question: Choose: 'She ___ pay for the meal — her boss did.'
questions.explanation: 'Didn't have to' → AUSENCIA de obligación pasada (no era necesario). Ojo: NO significa prohibición. Errores: (B) 'shouldn't have' es arrepentimiento; (C) 'hadn't to' no existe en inglés estándar; (D) mezcla imposible de estructuras.
examples: I didn't have to cook — my mum did it, thankfully. → no era necesario
We didn't have to buy tickets — they were free. → obligación inexistente

questions.statement: 'Shouldn't have + past participle' expresses criticism or regret about a past action.
questions.explanation: VERDADERO. 'Shouldn't have + participio' expresa CRÍTICA o ARREPENTIMIENTO por algo que SÍ se hizo pero no debería haberse hecho. 'Should have + participio' es lo opuesto: algo que NO se hizo pero debería haberse hecho.
examples: You shouldn't have said that — it really upset her. → crítica por algo hecho
I should have called earlier — I feel terrible. → arrepentimiento por algo no hecho

questions.text: You should have told me you were coming; I could have prepared dinner.
questions.explanation: Nota la contracción típica 'you should've told' /ʃʊdəv/ en habla — a menudo mal escrito como 'should of' (¡error!). 'Could have prepared' con el mismo patrón. Estructura clásica de reproche amable + oportunidad perdida: 'should have + PP + could have + PP'.
examples: I should have studied more for the exam — my own fault. → arrepentimiento propio
You should have listened to my advice — I warned you. → reproche + prueba

questions.prompt: Llegas tarde a una cita y das una explicación.
questions.question: Complete: 'I'm sorry I'm late. I ___ finish something at work.'
questions.explanation: 'Had to' → obligación pasada que justifica el retraso. Es la forma pasada natural de 'have to'. 'Should have' sería arrepentimiento (no encaja); 'must' no tiene pasado; 'didn't have to' invertiría el sentido.
examples: I had to answer an urgent email — sorry! → obligación + disculpa
She had to catch an earlier train, so she couldn't wait. → necesidad + consecuencia

questions.prompt: Empareja cada estructura con su significado exacto:

pairs.right: no obligation (I might not have done it)

questions.explanation: Cuatro formas clave para hablar del pasado: (1) had to = obligación cumplida; (2) didn't have to = ausencia de obligación; (3) should have = arrepentimiento por lo no hecho; (4) shouldn't have = crítica por lo hecho mal. No confundir 'didn't have to' con 'couldn't' (prohibido).
examples: I had to work late — no choice. → obligación cumplida
I shouldn't have shouted, honestly — I regret it. → crítica autoinfligida

questions.prompt: Le comentas a un amigo con cara de sueño por qué está tan cansado.
questions.question: Choose: 'You look tired. You ___ stayed up so late.'
questions.explanation: 'Shouldn't have stayed' → crítica constructiva sobre una decisión pasada equivocada. La lógica: hiciste algo (staying up late) que fue una mala idea. 'Should have' sería lo contrario; 'must have' es deducción; 'didn't have to' no encaja el reproche.
examples: You shouldn't have eaten so much cake — no wonder you feel sick. → crítica + consecuencia
He shouldn't have driven after drinking — dangerous move. → reproche moral

questions.target: Honestly, I should have listened to your advice — you were completely right.
questions.explanation: Situación: reconoces un error ante un amigo que te aconsejó bien. 'Should have + participio' expresa arrepentimiento sincero. 'Honestly' + reconocimiento explícito ('you were completely right') es muy natural para admitir errores. Muy útil para disculpas maduras.
examples: I should have called you sooner, honestly — I feel awful about it. → disculpa + emoción
I should have studied harder for the exam, no excuses. → autocrítica limpia

questions.statement: 'Didn't have to do it' means it was forbidden to do it.
questions.explanation: FALSO. 'Didn't have to' significa 'NO ERA NECESARIO' (podía hacerlo o no, libre elección). Para PROHIBICIÓN pasada se usa 'couldn't' o 'wasn't allowed to'. Este error es TOP-2 en hispanohablantes por confusión con 'no tenía que' (que puede sonar a prohibición).
examples: I didn't have to work — it was optional. → ausencia de obligación
I wasn't allowed to work — it was against the rules. → prohibición

questions.prompt: La reunión de las 9 se canceló a última hora y te enteras de camino.
questions.question: Complete: 'The meeting was cancelled, so we ___ go to the office.'
questions.explanation: Al cancelarse la reunión, dejó de ser necesario ir → 'didn't have to' expresa la ausencia de obligación. 'Had to' sería lo opuesto; 'shouldn't have' es arrepentimiento; 'must' no tiene pasado.
examples: It was Sunday, so we didn't have to work — pure luxury. → ausencia + valoración
The exam was postponed, so we didn't have to study that night. → causa + efecto

questions.text: I had to wake up at five to catch my early flight to London.
questions.explanation: Nota la fluidez 'had-to-wake-up' — la /d/ de 'had' se enlaza con la /t/ de 'to' casi como una sola consonante /dt/. 'At five' se pronuncia con weak form 'at'. 'Had to + infinitivo + to + finalidad' es estructura muy común para justificar obligaciones pasadas.
examples: She had to leave early to pick up her son from school. → obligación + causa
We had to save for years to buy this house — worth every penny. → esfuerzo + logro

questions.prompt: Identifica la frase que expresa arrepentimiento claro.
questions.question: Which sentence expresses regret?
options: I didn't have to work yesterday.
questions.explanation: 'Should have worked' → arrepentimiento: no lo hice pero debería haberlo hecho. Es LA forma clásica para lamentos pasados. (A) es obligación pasada neutra; (B) es ausencia de obligación; (D) es presente/futuro.
examples: I should have saved more money — regret it now. → lamento financiero
I should have accepted the offer, honestly. → arrepentimiento profesional

questions.statement: 'Must' has no past form, so we use 'had to' to talk about past obligation.
questions.explanation: VERDADERO. 'Must' es un modal DEFECTIVO — no tiene forma pasada propia. Para obligaciones pasadas usamos 'had to' (forma pasada de 'have to'). Ejemplos que NO existen: '*musted*', '*had must*'. Solo funciona 'must' en presente/futuro; 'had to' en pasado.
examples: Present: I must leave now, sorry. → obligación presente
Past: I had to leave early yesterday. → obligación pasada

questions.prompt: Regañas a un compañero de piso por un descuido peligroso.
questions.question: Complete: 'You ___ have left the door open! Anyone could have come in.'
questions.explanation: 'Shouldn't have left' → crítica sobre una acción pasada equivocada. La consecuencia potencial ('anyone could have come in') refuerza la crítica. 'Should have' sería lo opuesto; 'must have' es deducción; 'didn't have to' no encaja.
examples: You shouldn't have shouted at her — she was already stressed. → reproche + contexto
You shouldn't have told him the secret — now everyone knows! → crítica + consecuencia

questions.target: I had to work overtime last week, but honestly, I didn't have to come in on Saturday, thankfully.
questions.explanation: Situación: cuentas tu semana laboral a un amigo. Contraste clásico: 'had to' (obligación cumplida) + 'didn't have to' (ausencia de obligación). 'Honestly' + 'thankfully' añaden matices emocionales muy naturales. Perfecto para hablar de rutinas laborales.
examples: I had to study for exams all week, but I didn't have to work at least. → equilibrio
We had to book a table, but we didn't have to pay in advance — nice surprise. → norma + excepción
